explanation: Keep the three largest entries and the two smallest entries during one pass. Compare the product of the largest three with the product of the largest entry and the two smallest entries.
correctness: The extrema track occurrences, not distinct values, so equal entries can fill multiple slots. With a positive factor, the best remaining pair is either the two largest positives or the two most negative values. If every value is nonpositive, the three largest values give the least-negative product (or zero). Thus one of the two candidate products is optimal, including all-negative and zero cases.
walkthrough: For [-8,-5,2,4], the final three largest entries are 4,2,-5 and the two smallest are -8,-5. The candidate products are 4*2*(-5)=-40 and 4*(-8)*(-5)=160. Return 160; keeping only the three largest entries would lose the winning negative pair.
edgeCases: For [-6,-3,-2,-1], return -6, even though it is negative. Equal values at different positions remain distinct eligible factors.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: one pass maintains a fixed set of extrema with constant work per value.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: the extrema and candidate product are scalars; the input is never sorted or copied.
